--- title: "Where to Find Data Science Resources: A Practical Map 🧭" description: "A guided map of the best free places to learn data science, find datasets, copy real projects and industry use cases, and stay current, with a resource finder and a learning-loop simulation." author: "MLStation" date: 2026-10-01 categories: [Resources, Learning, Projects] draft: false --- The internet has more data science material than anyone could read in a lifetime. The problem is not finding something; it is finding the **right thing for where you are now**. This page is a map: what kind of resource to use for which goal, the best free places for each, and a simple loop that turns reading into real skill. 🚀 ::: {.callout-tip} ## 🎯 What you will get - A map of six resource types and the best free sources for each - A resource finder: pick your goal and level, get a short list - Where to find **real projects and industry use cases** to copy and adapt - The learn → build → share loop, and a simulation of why projects beat passive reading ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} ## 📚 The Resources hub [🧭 Overview: where to find resources](/resources/resources-overview.qmd) · [🛤️ Learning paths](/resources/learning-paths/industrial-use-case-paths.qmd) · [📝 Cheat sheets](/resources/cheat-sheets/data-science-cheat-sheets.qmd) · [📖 Glossary](/resources/glossary/data-science-glossary.qmd) · [🗄️ 20 open data sources](/resources/datasets/open-data-sources.qmd) · 📄 Paper notes (coming soon) ::: ## 🗺️ The six kinds of resources | | Type | Use it to | Best free starting points | |---|---|---|---| | 📘 | **Courses and books** | Learn concepts in order | [Kaggle Learn](https://www.kaggle.com/learn), [fast.ai](https://course.fast.ai/), [ISLP book](https://www.statlearning.com/), [Elements of Statistical Learning](https://hastie.su.domains/ElemStatLearn/) | | 🗄️ | **Datasets** | Practise on real data | [Kaggle Datasets](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets), [UCI repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/), [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/datasets), see our [20 open data sources](/resources/datasets/open-data-sources.qmd) | | 🏭 | **Projects and use cases** | See how real problems are framed and solved | Kaggle competitions and notebooks, company engineering blogs, our [learning paths](/resources/learning-paths/industrial-use-case-paths.qmd) | | 💻 | **Code and curated lists** | Reuse working code | [awesome-datascience](https://github.com/academic/awesome-datascience), library docs and example galleries | | 📄 | **Papers** | Understand state of the art | [Hugging Face Trending Papers](https://huggingface.co/papers/trending) (the old Papers with Code address now points here), arXiv | | 🧾 | **Quick references** | Look things up fast | Our [cheat sheets](/resources/cheat-sheets/data-science-cheat-sheets.qmd) and [glossary](/resources/glossary/data-science-glossary.qmd) | : Resource map {#tbl-map} ::: {.callout-note} ## 📝 Note The address `paperswithcode.com` now shows Hugging Face's **Trending Papers** page, which lists recent papers with their GitHub and arXiv links ([Papers with Code](https://paperswithcode.com/), [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/papers/trending)). Older tutorials that link to Papers with Code leaderboards may be out of date. ::: ## 🔎 Resource finder Tell us what you want to do and how far along you are. ```{ojs} //| echo: false import {ms, project", label: "I want to"}) viewof level = Inputs.radio(["🌱 Beginner", "🌿 Intermediate", "🌳 Advanced"], {value: "🌱 Beginner", label: "My level"}) ``` ```{ojs} //| echo: false finder = ({ "📘 Learn a `; } ``` ## 🏭 Where to find real projects and use cases Courses teach tools. **Use cases teach judgment**: how a business problem becomes a prediction, which metric matters and what "good enough" looks like. Four places are worth your time: 1. 🏆 **Kaggle competitions and notebooks.** Each competition starts with a business framing, a dataset and a metric. The top public notebooks show many solutions to the same problem. 2. 🏢 **Company engineering blogs.** Netflix, Uber, Airbnb, Spotify, DoorDash and others describe how they built recommendation, pricing, forecasting and fraud systems. Read them for the **problem framing and architecture**, not the code. 3. 🧰 **Curated GitHub lists.** [awesome-datascience](https://github.com/academic/awesome-datascience) collects learning resources, tools, datasets and communities in one README. 4. 🛤️ **Structured paths.** Our [learning paths](/resources/learning-paths/industrial-use-case-paths.qmd) turn eight industry problems (churn, fraud, forecasting, maintenance and more) into step-by-step projects with open datasets. ::: {.callout-important} ## ⚠️ Copy, then change one thing Re-running someone else's notebook teaches little. Rebuild it from scratch, then **change one thing**: a new dataset, a new metric, a new deployment target. That change is where the learning happens. ::: ## 🔁 The learning loop ```{mermaid} %%| echo: false flowchart LR A["📘 Learn
one concept"] --> B["🗄️ Practise
on a dataset"] B --> C["🏗️ Build
a small project"] C --> D["📣 Share
notebook, blog, repo"] D --> E["💬 Feedback
reviews, questions"] E --> A ``` Why does building matter so much? The simulation below follows two learners for 24 weeks. Both study 6 hours a week. **Learner A** only reads and watches. **Learner B** spends half the time on small projects. Press **▶ Play**. ::: {#cell-fig-loop .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"} import numpy as np, plotly.graph_objects as go from ms_charts import COLORS, PLOTLY_CONFIG rng = np.random.default_rng(1) weeks = np.arange(0, 25) def learner(project_share, forget): s, out = 5.0, [] for w in weeks: out.append(s) gain = 6 * (1 - project_share) * 0.9 + 6 * project_share * 1.6 * (1 + s / 60) s = s + gain * (1 - s / 100) - forget * s + rng.normal(0, 0.6) return np.array(out) A = learner(0.0, 0.035) B = learner(0.5, 0.012) def frame(k): return [go.Scatter(x=weeks[:k + 1], y=A[:k + 1], name="A: reading only", line=dict(color=COLORS["rose"], width=3.5)), go.Scatter(x=weeks[:k + 1], y=B[:k + 1], name="B: half projects", line=dict(color=COLORS["teal"], width=3.5))] fig = go.Figure(data=frame(0), frames=[go.Frame(data=frame(k), name=str(k)) for k in weeks]) fig.update_layout( height=400, xaxis=dict(range=[0, 24], title="Week"), yaxis=dict(range=[0, 100], title="Skill score (0–100, simulated)"), legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.14), updatemenus=[dict(type="buttons", x=0, y=-0.2, xanchor="left", showactive=False, buttons=[dict(label="▶ Play", method="animate", args=[None, dict(frame=dict(duration=180, redraw=False), fromcurrent=True, transition=dict(duration=120))]), dict(label="⏸ Pause", method="animate", args=[[None], dict(mode="immediate", frame=dict(duration=0))])])]) fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG) ``` ::: {#fig-loop .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` Simulated skill growth over 24 weeks. Passive study plateaus as unused knowledge is forgotten; project work keeps compounding. Illustrative model, not measured data. ::: ::: After 24 weeks the simulated project learner scores **89** vs **56** for the reader. The numbers are made up, but the shape matches common experience: knowledge you **use** sticks. ## 🗓️ A sample week A realistic plan for someone with a job, at 6 hours a week: ::: {#cell-fig-week .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code code-fold="true"} parts = ["📘 Learn a concept", "🗄️ Explore a dataset", "🏗️ Build the project", "📣 Write it up", "💬 Read others' work"] hours = [1.5, 1.0, 2.0, 1.0, 0.5] fig = go.Figure(go.Bar(x=hours, y=parts, orientation="h", text=[f"{h} h" for h in hours], textposition="outside", marker_color=[COLORS["indigo"], COLORS["violet"], COLORS["teal"], COLORS["amber"], COLORS["slate"]])) fig.update_layout(height=300, xaxis=dict(title="Hours", range=[0, 2.6]), yaxis=dict(autorange="reversed"), showlegend=False) fig.show(config=PLOTLY_CONFIG) ``` ::: {#fig-week .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` A balanced 6-hour learning week. ::: ::: ## ✅ A quick checklist for judging any resource | Question | Good sign 👍 | Warning sign 👎 | |---|---|---| | Is it current? | Updated in the last year or two, recent library versions | Old APIs, deprecated functions | | Does it show code and reasoning? | Explains why each step is done | Copy-paste code only | | Is the data real or realistic? | Messy data, missing values handled | Perfectly clean toy data only | | Does it measure results honestly? | Hold-out test set, clear metric | Accuracy on training data | | Can you run it? | Notebook or repo you can open | Screenshots only | ## 🧩 Summary - Use the **right resource type** for the goal: courses for concepts, datasets for practice, use cases for judgment. - Start with **free, high-quality sources**: Kaggle, UCI, ISLP, fast.ai, Hugging Face, awesome lists. - **Build, share, get feedback**, and repeat. Projects compound; passive reading fades. - Continue with [learning paths](/resources/learning-paths/industrial-use-case-paths.qmd) 🛤️, [cheat sheets](/resources/cheat-sheets/data-science-cheat-sheets.qmd) 📝, the [glossary](/resources/glossary/data-science-glossary.qmd) 📖 and [20 open data sources](/resources/datasets/open-data-sources.qmd) 🗄️.
